summary: Verified the Google Places autocomplete race-condition fix in AddressAutocomplete.jsx. All six scenarios in the review request PASS: (1) /measure input surfaces 5 suggestions for '1600 Amph' within ~2s with first suggestion being '1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA, USA'; (2) clicking suggestion-0 populates input with full formatted address '1600 Amphitheatre Pkwy, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA' and closes dropdown; (3) race-condition test — reloaded /measure and typed immediately (AutocompleteService was NOT yet ready at typing start), dropdown still appeared with 5 suggestions once library attached, confirming pendingInputRef latch works; (4) <3-char guard '12' yields 0 suggestions, '12 M' yields 5; (5) /customers/new cf-address field returns identical 5 suggestions; (6) zero TypeError / undefined / REQUEST_DENIED errors in console — only benign Google deprecation notices about legacy AutocompleteService (informational, not blocking).
action_items: Optional (informational, non-blocking): Google logs deprecation warnings that AutocompleteService and PlacesService are legacy per March 2025 notice. Consider migrating to AutocompleteSuggestion + Place classes at some future point (12+ month notice window; no user-facing impact today).
critical_code_review_comments: AddressAutocomplete.jsx fix is sound: awaits importLibrary('places') post-onload plus a 5s polling fallback, and pendingInputRef.current latches pre-ready keystrokes and is flushed in the ready-effect. This correctly closes the race window from iteration_12.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Google Places autocomplete verified working on /measure and /customers/new. Uses REACT_APP_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY. Bug from iteration_12 (svcRef staying null due to loading=async race) is fully resolved.
rca of the issue: Fixed in prior code change — verified in this iteration. Root cause was bootstrap onload firing before places sub-lib attached; fix awaits importLibrary('places') + polls AutocompleteService + latches early keystrokes in pendingInputRef.
